Are you looking for a Learning Support Assistant (LSA) role?

Do you have experience supporting children with ADHD, SEMH or challenging behaviour and feel confident managing difficult situations calmly and consistently?

Would you travel to a primary school in Lewisham?

If you answered YES, then this Learning Support Assistant role could be the perfect opportunity for you!

The Position - Learning Support Assistant

A highly regarded primary school is seeking a dedicated and resilient Learning Support Assistant (LSA) to join their team from 7th September. This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced LSA, Teaching Assistant or Behaviour Support Worker to provide dedicated support to a Year 6 pupil with ADHD and SEMH needs. The pupil can present with verbally challenging behaviour and may struggle with emotional regulation, transitions and returning to lessons. At times, they may abscond from the classroom or refuse to come back into the school building following break or lunchtime. As the LSA, you will work closely with the pupil throughout the school day, helping them regulate their emotions, manage challenging situations and access their learning in a safe and positive way. The successful candidate will be calm, patient, resilient and confident when managing challenging behaviour. Previous experience supporting children with ADHD, SEMH, behavioural needs or emotional regulation difficulties would be highly desirable.

The School - Learning Support Assistant

This welcoming primary school in Lewisham has been rated Outstanding by Ofsted and provides a supportive and inclusive environment for its pupils.You will be joining an experienced and dedicated staff team who work collaboratively to support pupils' academic, social and emotional development.The school is committed to ensuring that pupils receive the individualised support they need to overcome barriers to learning and make positive progress.

Apply today for this Learning Support Assistant role , or contact Millie at Qualiteach for more information.

company: LB Barking and Dagenham - Agency - Permanent
description:
Best Start Inclusion Early Language & Communication Support Worker

Ref: COMM00364

Contract Type: Fixed Term - 28 Months

Salary: £36,693

?About this job

As a Best Start Early Language and Communication Support Worker, you will play a key role in helping children aged 0 to 5 develop the speech, language and communication skills they need to thrive. Working as part of the Best Start multidisciplinary Inclusion Team, you will deliver evidence-based early intervention programmes and practical support to families across Barking and Dagenham.

You will lead the delivery of community-based Peep programmes, facilitate group sessions, provide one-to-one support to families and help create positive home learning environments that promote communication, confidence, independence and school readiness. Working in partnership with Family Hubs, early years settings, schools, health professionals and community organisations, you will support children and families to achieve improved outcomes through inclusive and preventative approaches.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about early childhood development and wants to make a lasting difference in the lives of children and families within their local community.

Special requirements for this post
- Ability to travel across Barking and Dagenham to deliver services and community-based programmes in a range of settings.
- Ability to work in a predominantly face-to-face community role, including delivering group programmes and family support sessions across the borough.
- Willingness to undertake Peeple Practitioner accreditation within the first three months of employment and deliver programmes in accordance with the accredited model.
- Commitment to safeguarding children and identifying and escalating concerns in line with local safeguarding procedures.
- Commitment to maintaining accurate records and working in accordance with GDPR, information governance and confidentiality requirements.

About you

We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated individual who is passionate about improving outcomes for young children and families. You will have experience of working with children, families or communities and understand the importance of early intervention in supporting speech, language and communication development.

You will be able to engage and motivate families, build positive relationships with professionals and partner organisations, and deliver activities that are inclusive, creative and responsive to the needs of children and families. You will have an understanding of child development, the importance of play and the home learning environment, and the key factors that support nursery and school readiness.

Ideally, you will hold a Level 3 qualification in Early Years, Child Development, Education, SEND, Health, Social Care or a related field, or have equivalent relevant experience. You will be organised, able to maintain accurate records and outcome data, confident using Microsoft Office applications, and committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Most importantly, you will be passionate about helping children develop the skills, confidence and foundations they need for a successful future.

About us

Barking & Dagenham is changing. It Starts Here.

Think you know Barking and Dagenham? Think again. While this small corner of east London might have a reputation for needing development, scratch beneath the surface and you'll find active communities and a place that consistently punches above its weight. The borough is changing - and changing for the better. And It Starts Here.

Yes, the borough has its challenges. But it's on the cusp of something exciting. With one of the youngest populations in the country, ambitions are high and rightly so. 98% of our schools are rated Good or Outstanding and every year more of our talented teenagers get into Russell Group Universities and hotly sought after apprenticeship schemes.

We have award winning parks, centuries old manor houses full of relics and artifacts you can go and see, and the ruins of one of Anglo-Saxon England's most powerful and wealthiest religious sites. We're even bringing beavers and white storks to the borough to help rewild the local landscape and boost biodiversity.

Over the past few years, we've been working hard to improve how we deliver services and support our community. From tackling inequality to making sure our services are the best they can be, we're focused on what matters most to local people.

We're creating the conditions for people to thrive - so everyone can enjoy a good quality of life, feel proud to call this place home, and be part of something bigger.

title: Inclusion Support Worker
company: LB Barking and Dagenham - Agency - Permanent
description:
Best Start Inclusion Support Worker

Ref: COMM00365

Contract Type: Fixed Term - 28 Months

Salary: £31,290

About this job

As a Best Start Inclusion Support Worker, you will play a vital frontline role in supporting children aged 0-5 and their families through the Best Start Family Hubs. Working alongside the Best Start Inclusion Practitioner, you will help identify emerging developmental and SEND needs at an early stage, support the delivery of targeted interventions, and promote inclusive practice across a range of community- based services.

You will co-deliver inclusive Stay and Play sessions, home learning and nursery readiness programmes, and provide practical support to children and families to improve developmental outcomes. Through your work, you will help create welcoming and accessible environments where all children can participate, thrive and reach their full potential.

This is an exciting opportunity to make a real difference to the lives of children and families by promoting inclusion, strengthening home learning environments and supporting children's communication, independence and school readiness.

Special requirements for this post
- Ability to travel across Barking and Dagenham to support the delivery of services, activities and community-based programmes.
- Ability to work in a predominantly face-to-face community-based role.
- Commitment to safeguarding children and working in line with safeguarding policies and procedures.
- Ability to work flexibly across Family Hub locations and community settings to meet the needs of children and families.
- Commitment to maintaining accurate records and adhering to GDPR, confidentiality and information governance requirements.

About you

You will be passionate about supporting young children and families and committed to ensuring every child has the best possible start in life. You will have experience of working with children, families or communities and an understanding of early intervention approaches that improve outcomes for children.

You will have knowledge of child development and be able to support children with a range of developmental and additional needs. You will be confident engaging families, delivering group activities and building positive relationships with children, parents, colleagues and partner organisations.

Ideally, you will hold a Level 3 qualification in Early Years, Child Development, Education, Health, Social Care or a related discipline, or have equivalent relevant experience. You will be organised, able to maintain accurate records, confident using Microsoft Office applications, and committed to equality, diversity and inclusion.

Most importantly, you will be enthusiastic about helping children develop the communication, independence and social skills they need to flourish at home, in early years settings and beyond.

About us

Barking & Dagenham is changing. It Starts Here.

Think you know Barking and Dagenham? Think again. While this small corner of east London might have a reputation for needing development, scratch beneath the surface and you'll find active communities and a place that consistently punches above its weight. The borough is changing - and changing for the better. And It Starts Here.

Yes, the borough has its challenges. But it's on the cusp of something exciting. With one of the youngest populations in the country, ambitions are high and rightly so. 98% of our schools are rated Good or Outstanding and every year more of our talented teenagers get into Russell Group Universities and hotly sought after apprenticeship schemes.

We have award winning parks, centuries old manor houses full of relics and artifacts you can go and see, and the ruins of one of Anglo-Saxon England's most powerful and wealthiest religious sites. We're even bringing beavers and white storks to the borough to help rewild the local landscape and boost biodiversity.

Over the past few years, we've been working hard to improve how we deliver services and support our community. From tackling inequality to making sure our services are the best they can be, we're focused on what matters most to local people.

We're creating the conditions for people to thrive - so everyone can enjoy a good quality of life, feel proud to call this place home, and be part of something bigger.
- with our streets, our schools, our neighbourhoods. And with your application to join our determined team who are passionate about doing what's best for the future of Barking and Dagenham.

As an Investors in People Gold Award employer, we're serious about supporting our staff. From flexible working, professional training and career development to wellbeing initiatives, we want our people to feel valued and supported in everything they do.

Additional Information

We're committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. If you require any adjustments or support at any stage, please contact the Hiring Manager to discuss your needs.

title: Support Worker
description:
Urban Care Community Limited is an introductory company that connects Clients and Care Professionals to deliver cost-effective and better care. We are currently seeking a workforce requirement for a highly skilled and compassionate Self-Employed Support Worker/ Carer who possesses experience and expertise in managing individuals with Learning Disabilities, Autism spectrum disorder (ASD), Mental Health Disorders, Communication Disorders, Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Physical Disabilities, Challenging Behaviour, Epilepsy and Diabetes Management.

Key Responsibilities:

1. A Support Worker must provide direct care and support to individuals with Learning Disabilities, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Mental Health Disorders, Communication Disorders, Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Physical Disabilities, Challenging Behaviour, Epilepsy and Diabetes Management.

2. A Support Worker must develop and implement personalised care plans in collaboration with the individual and their families, ensuring that their unique needs and preferences are considered.

3. A Support Worker must assist in the management and monitoring of medication administration, adhering to prescribed protocols and maintaining accurate records.

4. A Support Worker must employ effective intervention strategies to manage challenging behaviors and promote positive outcomes for the individuals in our care.

5. Foster a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment to promote the physical, emotional, and social well-being of our clients.

6. Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team, including medical professionals, therapists, and educational staff, to ensure the holistic care and development of each individual.

7. Maintain accurate and up-to -date documentation, including progress notes, incident reports, Challenging behaviour chart, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and organisational protocols.

Required Skills and Qualifications:

1. Minimum of 2 years of experience working with individuals with learning Disabilities, Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Mental Health Disorders, Communication Disorders, Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD),Physical Disabilities, Challenging Behaviour, Epilepsy and Diabetes Management

2. Knowledge and understanding of best practices in supporting individuals with complex needs, including behavior management techniques, medication administration and crisis intervention.

3. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport and establish effective relationships with individuals, families and co-workers.

4. Ability to work independently, prioritise tasks and adapt to changing environments and needs.

5. Hold relevant certifications or qualifications in related field is preferred but not required.

6. Empathy, patience and a genuine passion for working with individuals who have diverse needs.

8. Flexibility in working hours, as the role may require occasional evenings, weekends, or overnight shifts.

9. Basic digital skills for documentation purposes.

Your Benefits:
- Free Uniform provided
- Free Level 2 or 3 Qualification in Helath and Social Care.

If you are passionate about making a positive impact in the lives of others and have a desire to help individuals with disabilities or special needs achieve their goals, we encourage you to apply for the position of Self-employed Support Worker. We offer competitive compensation and opportunities for professional growth within our organisation.
